Reader

Reading · defined at reader.mbt:37

pub(all) struct Reader {
  view : BytesView
  config : Config
  mut at : Int32
  refs : Array[Int32]
  nodes : Map[Int32, Value]
  schemas : Map[Int32, StructMeta]
  mut replay : Int32
  replaying : Array[Int32]
  mut depth : Int32
  mut spent : Int32
}

Where a value comes from: the bytes, the place in them, and what has been read already.

The mirror of Writer. A reader keeps two things about references: where each one started, so a value can be read again, and the container being built for each one, so a cycle can point at a value that is not finished.

Fields

FieldMeaning
view : BytesView

The bytes being read.

config : Config

What this message is read under.

mut at : Int32

Where the next byte is.

refs : Array[Int32]

Where the value of each reference id starts.

nodes : Map[Int32, Value]

The container being built for each reference id, before it is filled.

schemas : Map[Int32, StructMeta]

The structs this reader knows, by the user type ID they are registered under: same-schema mode is an agreement, and this is where it is kept.

mut replay : Int32

How deep in a replay this read is: a value being read a second time for a reference does not get a reference id of its own.

replaying : Array[Int32]

The offsets of the replays above this one, so a cycle is caught rather than read for ever.

mut depth : Int32

How deep in the nesting this read is.

mut spent : Int32

How many bytes of variable-length payload have been declared so far.

Methods

end

fn Reader::end(Self) -> Unit raise

Refuse the bytes left over once a value has been read.

A message with two values in it is two messages, and reading one of them and ignoring the rest is how a truncation goes unnoticed.

enter

fn Reader::enter(Self) -> Unit raise

Go one level deeper, refusing a message nested past what was configured.

enter_ref

fn Reader::enter_ref(Self, Int32) -> Int32 raise

Go back to where the value of reference id was written and read it again, which is what a reference asks for when the value was not a container put aside. The answer is the offset to hand to leave_ref afterwards.

A reference that points into a value still being read is a cycle this package cannot rebuild — a MoonBit value is finished before it is held — so it is refused rather than read until the stack runs out.

new

fn Reader::new(Bytes, config? : Config, schemas? : Array[StructMeta]) -> Self

A reader at the start of bytes, knowing the structs named in schemas.

A struct arrives as a user type ID and nothing else, so the schema it stands for has to be given to the reader before it is met.

node

fn Reader::node(Self, Int32) -> Value?

The container being built for a reference id, when there is one.

A cycle points at a value that is not finished, so the container is put here before its contents are read, and the reference finds it.
